key_insight: A DFT-informed, all-atom model reproduces key experimental features of the resorcinol-formaldehyde aerogel skeleton and enables simulation of iron incorporation.
engineering_relevance: The model provides a starting point for screening fillers and dopants for RF aerogels, including prospective thermoelectric functionalization.
method: Optimize the RF base unit with DFT and compare its infrared spectrum with experiment.
Benchmark classical force fields against DFT for branched RF structures and select COMPASS II.
Equilibrate a 15,012-atom skeleton using NVT/NPT molecular dynamics, then simulate 5 wt% iron addition.
evidence_signal: Calculated infrared spectra agreed with experiment, simulated skeletal density was 1.296 versus 1.3 g/cm³ experimentally, and embedded iron increased from 63% to 71% over 1 ns.
watch_item: The model aggregates RF units without inter-unit cross-links; longer-term dopant stability and functional properties remain to be validated.
paper_title: An All-Atom Model of the Resorcinol-Formaldehyde Aerogel Skeleton from DFT and Molecular Dynamics: Validation and Iron Incorporation
